llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Chinese course-generation workflow that uses scoped local files and a read-only verifier, with no evidence of hidden network, credential, persistence, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: Local read/write access is proportionate to generating course markdown, manifests, optional local config, and explicit archiving; the skill states it does not need network, credentials, or external services.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no hidden installer or dependency fetch. The only elevated command text is a Linux example for installing python3, not a command the skill automatically runs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions limit reads to user-specified material ranges, write only to specified or disclosed local output directories, keep source materials read-only in generation mode, and require user confirmation before overwrites, moves, or ambiguous course boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background workers, scheduled tasks, credential/session access, memory writes, or persistent hooks were found. Optional local config and course outputs are user-directed artifacts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to turn user-provided transcripts or documents into structured course files, optionally archive courses on explicit request, and extract training plans from verified material; the file generation, manifest creation, and verification scripts fit that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable with a Chinese-language workflow that reads user-selected course materials and writes generated course files locally. Review the output directory before archiving, and only run the self-test if you are intentionally validating the verifier rather than generating a course.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The self-test behavior is real but disclosed as development verification; the inspected script writes temporary fixtures under TemporaryDirectory, mutates only those fixtures, invokes the verifier with an explicit argv list, and cleans up automatically.
[AE1] expected: The referenced verifier artifact was available in this workspace and fully inspected; it validates course directories, blocks path traversal in manifest paths, reads course files, and emits hashes without modifying course files.
[SQP-3] expected: The skill and examples are Chinese-language and require Chinese course-output structures. This is a usability/locale limitation to disclose, but it is coherent with the package presentation and not a security concern by itself.
[LP3] expected: The skill does use local file operations and a shell verifier entrypoint, but its instructions scope reads and writes to user-specified materials/output directories and require consent for overwrite or movement.
[PE2] unexpected: The sudo text is only an installation hint for a missing system python3 dependency; the verifier script does not request or execute sudo.
[AST4] expected: subprocess.run appears in the development self-test only, using sys.executable and an explicit argument list with shell=False behavior, not interpolated shell input.
[A.I.G SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G scan reported no security results.
